description: Golden table for the coordinate space a captured window's own box declares (#2612), the twin of tap-keyboard-occlusion-policy.json on the geometry that guard reads. iOS hosts some system surfaces in the device's native (portrait-up) space even while the app is rotated, so their whole subtree arrives quarter-turned: measured on iPhone 17 Pro (iOS 26.2) with the system keyboard up over a landscape app frame (0,0,874,402), UIRemoteKeyboardWindow reports its own box as (0,0,402,874) — the app's box with the two side lengths swapped — while the app's own UIWindow, UITextEffectsWindow and a dev-menu overlay window all report (0,0,874,402); in portrait the same keyboard window reports (0,0,402,874) against a (0,0,402,874) app frame, i.e. nothing is turned. RULE 1 (detection) is enforced twice, in packages/contracts/src/window-coordinate-space.ts and in SnapshotGeometrySpace inside apple/snapshot-presentation/Sources/AgentDeviceSnapshotPresentation/SnapshotCoordinateSpace.swift, and decides from side lengths alone: a window is quarter-turned relative to an app frame when the app frame is not square (abs(app.width - app.height) > quarterTurnTolerance), both frames are finite, positive and non-empty, and the window's side lengths match the app's on the swapped axes (abs(window.width - app.height) <= quarterTurnTolerance && abs(window.height - app.width) <= quarterTurnTolerance). Origins are deliberately never compared: the turn is a statement about which axis a box runs along, and a window may legitimately be placed elsewhere. A square app frame cannot be told from its own quarter turn, so it is left alone rather than guessed at. The tolerance is 1 because measured captures match the swap to the point and this absorbs float representation only. RULE 2 (rotation) is the capture's way back for the runner's own UIInterfaceOrientation raw values — 1 portrait, 2 portraitUpsideDown, 3 landscapeRight, 4 landscapeLeft, and 0 unknown, where portrait and unknown publish what the platform reported rather than inventing a turn — implemented by CoordinateSpaceRotation.oriented(rect:in:interfaceOrientation:) in that same Swift file, whose rect helper turns opposite corners of the reported box and re-orders them so the result keeps a top-left origin. `rotationCases` are native -> oriented rows: the landscape ones measured on the device above, the 180 degree and identity ones derived from that table. Capture turns back with the exact inverse of what dispatch turns forward, so each row also has to come back to its own `native` box under the forward mapping; that is why one measured-looking landscape-left pairing whose native and oriented boxes are identical is absent — the table computes no such row. Infinity has no JSON spelling, so the unusable frame a platform hands back when it could not resolve a box is named {"infinite": true} and decodes to CGRect.infinite on the Swift side and to an infinite rect on the TypeScript side. RULE 3 (content translation, #3899) is the one rule here that reads an origin: an iPad window placed off the screen origin (Windowed Apps, Stage Manager) reports its subtree from its own top-left — measured on iPad Pro 11-inch (M5, iOS 27.0), a Calendar window at screen (224,207,386x682) reports its root as (0,0,386,682) and its Add button as (335,14,37,36) for a control drawn at (559,221). SnapshotContentTranslation.offset(reportedBox:viewportBox:) names the viewport origin as the offset only when the carrier is a (0,0)-anchored box whose side lengths match the viewport's within the tolerance and the viewport starts elsewhere; any other carrier, such as the keyboard window or a SpringBoard overlay that report the screen's own box, and every window at the screen origin name none (null). `windowContentCases` replay against that Swift function alone, because the bridge guest refuses a windowed tree before the host decoder can read one. `rotationCases` pin the turn as axes-only: a non-zero app frame origin never travels through it.

quarterTurnCases.name: UIRemoteKeyboardWindow reports the app box with its side lengths swapped on a landscape iPhone
the app's own UIWindow reports the app's box, which is the space the capture publishes
UITextEffectsWindow tracks the interface rotation and reports the app's box too
a dev-menu overlay window reports the app's box and is not a native-hosted surface
portrait: the keyboard window and the app report the same box, so nothing is turned
a square app frame cannot be told from its own quarter turn, so its geometry is left alone
an app frame square to within the tolerance is not square enough to be turned back either
origins are not compared: a quarter-turned window elsewhere in an offset app frame still declares the native space
a window missing the swap by half a point is float representation, not a different box
a window missing the swap by more than the tolerance is some other box, and stays app space
an app frame the capture could not resolve has no box to compare against
a non-finite app frame anchors no rotation
a non-finite window box declares nothing
a zero-width window carries no geometry to read a space from

rotationCases.name: landscape right turns the reported key plane from a strip on the left edge into the band docked at the bottom
landscape right turns one reported key with its plane
landscape right turns the keyboard dock's own button into the strip below the keys
landscape right turns the keyboard window's own box onto the app's box
landscape right keeps a zero-area padding key zero-area at the plane's corner
a non-zero app frame origin does not travel through the turn: the same native box comes back at the same place (#3899)
landscape left turns the same plane the other way, which is where its own native column is
portrait publishes what the platform reported: the reported return key is the app's return key
an orientation the platform did not name rotates nothing, even for a landscape app frame
portrait upside down moves the reported box to the opposite corner without swapping its axes
Duo inner panel automation button: native digitizer to landscape window (measured UITouch)

windowContentCases.name: a Calendar window placed at (224,207) reports its subtree from its own top-left
the app's own window box reports the screen box it is placed at and translates nothing
a full-screen window — iPad, iPhone, or an ADR 0025 foldable panel — starts at (0,0) and translates nothing
a half-tolerance side-length miss is float representation, not a different box
a carrier two points narrower than the viewport is some other box and declares no space
an empty carrier names no box to translate
an empty viewport names no screen box to translate toward
